name: Sagarmatha
description: A star 49 parsecs away, 1.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56572: radius 1.062 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 0.872 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.048) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56572: effective temperature 5415 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.078)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 56572: distance 49.364 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.013), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 49 parsecs away, 1.1 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 0.872 times the Sun's luminosity at 5,415 K, so 1.062 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 56572: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: HD 100777
quotes.card: HD 100777 is a single star with a planetary companion in the equatorial constellation of Leo.
quotes.introduction: With an apparent visual magnitude of 8.42 it is too faint to be viewed with the naked eye, although the absolute magnitude of 4.81 indicates it could be seen if it were just 33 ly (10 pc) away.
